title: Yui draws its first six screens
body: An agent can now reply with a timer, a question, a multiple choice, a pick-several, a form or a list, and Yui draws it as a real card inside the chat instead of plain text. The timer counts rounds on a ring and beeps on the last three seconds. Forms handle text, numbers, dates, sliders, yes/no toggles and voice notes, and will not submit until the required fields are filled. Every tap goes back to the agent as one small event, and your answer shows up as your own chat bubble. All the styling comes from the same theme file, so a restyle changes these cards too. A hidden paste box lets us test any Yui Lines reply by hand. Build 9 is on TestFlight.

title: The wordmark moves into the app
body: Chris's hand-drawn Yui wordmark, the one with bunny-ear arms on the Y, now sits in the app's top bar, on the empty chat screen and in settings. Its coral is now the app's main color too: the send button, your chat bubbles and the selected toggle all use it, with the pastels kept for the smaller touches. The coral is stored in the same theme file as everything else, so an agent that restyles the app recolors the logo along with it. It reads clearly on both the cream light mode and the dark plum mode, so one logo file covers both. Yui the cat stays as the face of the agent. Build 8 is on TestFlight.

title: Yui Lines has a test suite
body: Yui Lines is the one-line format an agent uses to put a timer or a question on your screen. It now has a shared test suite: 165 small cases, each a bit of input plus the exact result a parser must return. The web playground's parser and the new Swift parser inside the app both pass every case, and any future parser, Android included, has to pass the same files. Writing the cases turned up a few gaps in the spec, such as what a mistyped form field should do. Those answers are now written down.

title: Yui gets a face
body: Yui now has a look: a round white cat named Yui, soft pastels on warm cream paper, rounded type, and a little bounce when you tap send. The feel borrows from Korean character apps like Kakao Friends: cute, but not childish. There is a light and dark mode with a toggle in settings. Under the hood every color, corner and animation lives in one small data file, so later an agent can restyle the whole app on the fly. Build 5 is on TestFlight with the new icon.

title: First TestFlight build
body: The Swift app exists. Build 4 is a bare SwiftUI chat screen with a placeholder icon, signed and uploaded to TestFlight straight from the build machine with no one opening Xcode. It does nothing useful yet. What matters is the pipeline: from here every change can reach a phone in minutes. First upload was rejected for a missing app icon, fixed in one commit.

title: Waitlist open
body: The waitlist is live on yuigui.com. Sign up for TestFlight invites and occasional updates. Signups land in a small table in PostScarcity AI's existing database, no new infrastructure.

title: Apple Developer account active
body: Yui has an Apple Developer account, so TestFlight is unblocked. Xcode is installing on the build machine. Next: the Swift project and an automatic TestFlight build on every push.

title: yuigui.com is live
body: The hub now lives at yuigui.com. Yui is built in public: this log updates as work ships, and a weekly update lands every Friday.

title: Stack decision: all Swift
body: Yui will be a native SwiftUI iPhone app, not React Native. The reason is the product: Yui should feel like part of the phone, and the features that set it apart (a workout timer on the lock screen, Siri and the Action button, Apple's on-device model and speech) are native Apple surfaces. The preset design keeps the app small, so an Android port later is a port of the presets, not a rewrite. No Apple Watch app yet. Yui Lines stays platform-neutral: the web playground and the Swift app parse it the same way.

title: Source on GitHub
body: The hub, roadmap, Yui Lines spec and benchmark now live at postscarcityai/yuigui. The app code gets its own repo, yui.

title: Yui Lines v0: spec, 12 presets, playground, token benchmark
body: Agents now speak Yui Lines: one short line per component, no UI code, no JSON. Spec at /yl, live playground at /playground with all 12 presets (timer, ask, choose, pick, slide, form, list, table, card, image, camera, mic), line-by-line streaming, ~patch, >screen routing, save/show and the custom {json} escape hatch. Benchmark on 10 screens with real tokenizers: YL is 1.6x smaller than minified JSON, 2.7x smaller than pretty JSON, 3.9x smaller than a component-tree document.

title: Hub site live (Phase 0)
body: This site: overview, roadmap, progress log, business plan draft, pitch deck, three phone mockups. Deployed to Vercel as project yui. yuigui.com not attached yet.

title: Roadmap v1
body: Six phases written from the pitch. Stack call: JSON UI protocol, Expo app, Cloudflare relay, Hermes connector. Arnold is the first agent wired in.

title: Pitch recorded and transcribed
body: Chris recorded a 21.6 minute pitch (rec 366). Transcribed locally with Whisper and summarized. The name settled on Yui.
